description: Rubric for dc-audit. Each rule is evaluated against a devcontainer.json. `check` is a jq expression that returns true when the rule FAILS (i.e., the condition indicates a problem). `fix` is applied only when `fixable: true` and --fix is passed; it is a jq program that receives the current document and must return the corrected document. Fixes must be additive and never overwrite existing values.

profiles.attended: Ergonomic dev profiles. Warns on the high-impact footguns (docker.sock, host credential mounts, privileged caps) so reviewers see them; doesn't block, since a human is in the loop.
profiles.unattended: Hardened profiles for autonomous runs. Strict capability drops, no credential mounts, resource caps, egress control expected. Same warn rules as attended apply; `--strict` is recommended in CI.

rules.message: `image` should include a tag or digest (floating names like `:debian` drift).
Must set either `image` or `dockerFile` / `build`.
rules.check: (.image // null) == null and (.build // null) == null and (.dockerFile // null) == null and (.dockerComposeFile // null) == null

rules.message: `features` keys should include a version suffix (e.g., `git:1` or `git:1.2.5`).

`git` feature resolves to a git older than {{MIN_GIT}}: no `version` (defaults to os-provided), explicit `os-provided`/`system`, or a pinned version below the floor. `extensions.relativeWorktrees` needs {{MIN_GIT}}, so per-worktree containers fail postCreate with `fatal: not in a git directory`. Set `"version": "latest"` (or pin >= {{MIN_GIT}}).
rules.check: def vnorm: split(".") | map(tonumber) | . + [0, 0, 0] | .[:3]; (.features // {}) | to_entries | map(select((.key | test("/git:")) and ((.value | if type == "object" then (.version // "os-provided") else tostring end) as $v | ($v | IN("os-provided", "system")) or (($v | test("^[0-9]+(\\.[0-9]+)*$")) and (($v | vnorm) < ($min_git | vnorm)))))) | length > 0

rules.message: Set `shutdownAction` so dangling containers do not accumulate.
Set `updateRemoteUserUID: true` for Codespaces-safe UID mapping.
`runArgs` should include `--security-opt=no-new-privileges`.
`runArgs` includes `--privileged`; the container can mount host filesystems and escape isolation. Remove it and add only the specific capabilities you need.
`runArgs` adds `SYS_ADMIN`; this capability is broad enough to enable namespace and mount manipulation. Prefer narrower caps (e.g. `NET_BIND_SERVICE`).
`runArgs` sets `--security-opt=seccomp=unconfined`; Docker's default seccomp profile blocks ~50 dangerous syscalls and disabling it widens the attack surface.
Set a `--pids-limit` in `runArgs` to bound forkbomb blast radius (recommend 2048).
Unattended profile must set `--pids-limit` (recommend 1024).
Unattended profile should set `--memory` in `runArgs` (recommend 8g).
Unattended profile should set `--cpus` in `runArgs` (recommend 4).
Unattended profile should `--cap-drop=ALL` and re-add only what is needed.
Unattended profile must not bind-mount host credential directories (~/.ssh, ~/.aws, ~/.config/gh, ~/.config/glab-cli, ~/.gnupg, ~/.kube, ~/.docker).

Bind-mounts a host credential directory (~/.ssh, ~/.aws, ~/.config/gh, ~/.config/glab-cli, ~/.gnupg, ~/.kube, ~/.docker). These are long-lived, high-value credentials -- every layer below this mount is bypassable through the mounted file. Confirm the mount is necessary and consider per-project narrowing.

Mounts `docker.sock`. The container can then spawn sibling containers as `--privileged`, mount host filesystems, and exfiltrate the host. Effectively grants root on the host -- prefer dind-rootless or a higher-trust boundary.

Mount source is `${localEnv:HOME}` with no subdirectory; the container can read every dotfile and credential in the host home directory. Pin to a specific subdirectory (e.g. `${localEnv:HOME}/.config/some-tool`).
Put fixed unattended flags (CLAUDE_UNATTENDED, RALPH_*) in `containerEnv`, not `remoteEnv` (remoteEnv can be unset by an in-container shell).
When `postCreateCommand` is set, declare `waitFor` explicitly (VS Code defaults vary).
Custom `workspaceMount` silently disables `--mount-git-worktree-common-dir` (devcontainers/cli#1243), so git breaks inside per-worktree containers. Prefer the default workspace mount.

Fixed volume name is shared by every container of this config, including per-worktree containers. Verify sharing is intended (credentials tolerate it; append-heavy state does not) or scope with ${devcontainerId}.
rules.check: (.mounts // []) | map(if type == "string" then . else (("source=" + (.source // "")) + ",type=" + (.type // "")) end) | map(select(test("type=volume") and (test("\\$\\{devcontainerId\\}|\\$\\{localWorkspaceFolder") | not))) | length > 0
